observations.statement: The excerpt makes blocked episodes canonical across several waiting causes and preserves an unresolved episode when restart makes its in-flight attempt historical.
Routing is centered on route_target, with resume_url treated as derived transport and shell layout intentionally excluded from route identity.
Receipts and projections are declared attempt-native, while the executor attribution packet mixes one required identifier with several optional identifiers.
The account model requires durable requested-versus-effective history and introduces a durable account-switch record with a closed decision-kind vocabulary.
Identity-native opens can resolve artifacts to transient generated buffers before persistence.
Command-dispatch proof is described as needing route and open normalization coverage, but the stated gate work is deferred.
Concern identity is explicitly separate from blocked episodes and is given four named lifecycle states in the following context.

candidate_findings.title: Restart recovery lacks a crash-safe transition protocol
candidate_findings.claim: The excerpt names resume, retry, wait, and stale-historical outcomes but does not define atomic ownership transfer, lease or epoch checks, retry idempotency, duplicate-side-effect handling, retry ceilings, backoff, or terminal escalation.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: A restart racing a still-live worker can duplicate execution or side effects, while an indefinitely retained blocked episode can remain actionable without a deterministic convergence path.

candidate_findings.title: Approval resolution lacks authority, concurrency, and replay rules
candidate_findings.claim: Approval identity and approver provenance are specified, but the excerpt does not define authorization predicates, conflict arbitration between approvers, compare-and-set or version semantics, duplicate-resolution behavior, replay rejection, or validation of a modified action against the blocked episode's ordered allowed actions.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: Concurrent, stale, or unauthorized approval responses could execute a different action than the prompt represented or resolve an episode that has already changed.

candidate_findings.title: Remediation compatibility mapping is required but not defined
candidate_findings.claim: The excerpt requires an explicit mapping between legacy and current remediation outcomes but supplies no mapping table, ambiguity rule for legacy failed, unknown-value handling, or deterministic replay behavior.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: History, recovery, and graph consumers can normalize the same legacy outcome differently, erasing distinctions the excerpt explicitly says must survive.

candidate_findings.title: Account-switch records lack decision-dependent invariants and ordering
candidate_findings.claim: The historical model requires a requested-side anchor, yet requested, source, destination, run, attempt, and thread identifiers are globally optional in account_switch_event. The excerpt gives no per-decision presence matrix, causal sequence, idempotency key, or total-order rule.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: A switched event can omit both endpoints, a blocked-required-account event can omit the requested account, and concurrent switches can become impossible to order or reconcile reliably.

candidate_findings.title: Executor attribution fields have no conditional presence rules
candidate_findings.claim: The executor-facing packet labels node_id, attempt_id, execution_role, provider_attempt_ref, and usage_event_ref as optional without defining when each becomes mandatory, despite attempt-native receipts and projections.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: A dispatch containing only run_id can appear conformant while being impossible to join to the responsible node, attempt, provider call, or usage record.

candidate_findings.title: Cross-scope routes lack authorization revalidation
candidate_findings.claim: Routes may override project, thread, run, panel, and tab scope, and persisted resume_url values decode back into route_target, but the excerpt states no authorization recheck, tenant-boundary constraint, scope-consistency validation, or rejection rule for stale or forged scope combinations.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: Opening a persisted or externally supplied route could reveal an object from a project, thread, or run the current actor is not authorized to inspect.

candidate_findings.title: Route migration has no deterministic compatibility protocol
candidate_findings.claim: Older payloads may be accepted and wrappers or aliases normalize to canonical contracts, but the excerpt defines no schema versions, canonicalization and round-trip rules, unknown-field behavior, decode failures, alias-cycle detection, telemetry, or retirement criteria.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: Different producers and resolvers can accept or reinterpret the same legacy payload differently, leaving migration failures silent and indefinitely preserving divergent route models.

candidate_findings.title: Transient generated buffers lack lifecycle and privacy controls
candidate_findings.claim: Transient generated artifact sources are valid before persistence, but the excerpt does not define ownership, access control, identifier collision handling, redaction or encryption, retention and cleanup, crash recovery, or the race when a real source appears while a generated buffer is open.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: Non-persisted drafts may contain sensitive material and can leak, disappear unexpectedly, resolve to the wrong artifact, or diverge from the subsequently persisted source.

candidate_findings.title: Attention projections can present contradictory GUI truth
candidate_findings.claim: project_attention_item combines active, optional resolved_at_utc, quiet_until_utc, dismissibility, and projection trust without a consistency matrix or transition authority. Storage owns freshness and fallback mechanics, but this excerpt gives no freshness threshold or required UI behavior for stale, unavailable, or conflicting projections.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: A UI can legitimately render an item as active, resolved, quieted, and stale at once, or silently hide urgent attention based on an obsolete projection.

candidate_findings.title: Critical route and command proof is deferred and underspecified
candidate_findings.claim: The excerpt says GATE-010 must eventually cover wrapper normalization, route_target pass-through, OpenSubject binding, and alias classification, but supplies no current executable oracle, negative cases, round-trip cases, idempotency checks, or migration corpus.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: The most compatibility-sensitive seam can be declared structurally wired while malformed routing, alias confusion, and failed subject resolution remain undetected.

candidate_findings.title: OpenSubject shape introduces an undefined required target_kind
candidate_findings.claim: OpenSubject is described with subject_id and open_intent, while later prose introduces a required target_kind without defining its values, relation to open_intent, or precedence against route_target destination overrides and restored project surface state.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: Callers can produce incompatible OpenSubject payloads or disagree about whether destination choice belongs to subject opening, route activation, or persisted shell state.

candidate_findings.title: Durable account lineage lacks privacy and retention policy
candidate_findings.claim: Requested and effective account identity is preserved across historical run, usage, approval, recovery, auth, graph, and artifact surfaces, but the excerpt defines no data classification, least-privilege view, masking, retention, deletion, export, or audit-access policy.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: Concrete account and provider identity can become broadly replicated durable personal or organizational data with no stated boundary on who can inspect it or how long it persists.

candidate_findings.title: Degraded-trust escalation lacks operational convergence rules
candidate_findings.claim: The excerpt requires degraded-trust and account-health escalation through concern, blocked-owner, and escalation-ladder models but does not specify trigger thresholds, hysteresis, deduplication, severity mapping, rate limits, recovery clearing, or behavior when the projection source is unavailable.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: Noisy health changes can create alert storms or duplicate concerns, while stale recovery state can leave users blocked or falsely reassured.

explicit_non_gaps.statement: The excerpt explicitly prevents request_id from becoming the primary approval target and anchors approval identity in the blocked episode.
Tier boundaries are explicitly rejected as approval scope anchors.
Route activation is explicitly prohibited from serializing layout geometry and full project-state snapshots.
The excerpt explicitly separates generated source transport from canonical persisted artifact identity.
Provider-account normalization explicitly preserves the github_api versus copilot_github realm boundary and separates transport host from upstream provider.
Concern records are explicitly distinct from blocked episodes and have named active, acknowledged, resolved, and dismissed lifecycle states.
Stable wrapper normalization is explicitly distinguished from deprecated alias mapping.
Durable requested-side account evidence is explicitly required beside effective execution identity.
The prose explicitly assigns operational identity to side-effecting records and requires it on effective-resolution records.

unknowns.reason_unresolved: The bounded excerpt references joint owners and recovery rules but does not include their executable schemas or transition tables.

unknowns.reason_unresolved: The evidence universe contains only high-level normalization and ownership prose.

unknowns.reason_unresolved: The excerpt establishes validity and resolution behavior but no operational buffer contract.

unknowns.reason_unresolved: The excerpt says the gate must eventually validate them but provides no current receipt or oracle.

unknowns.reason_unresolved: The excerpt assigns those mechanics to storage but does not expose their definitions.

exact_evidence_refs.excerpt: If restart determines an in-flight attempt cannot resume, that attempt transitions to `stale_historical`; if a blocked prerequisite still exists, the existing unresolved blocked episode remains the actionable state.
`/rules` decide whether recovery resumes, retries, or waits, while the owning blocked episode keeps attribution and restart intent visible to Executor, HITL, and stream consumers.
`HITL` request/resolution events carry actor/lane/account identity and approver provenance.

The canonical flow is the blocked/runtime overlay: `waiting_approval`, `/blocked`, `blocked_sequence`, ordered `allowed_action_ids[]` / `allowed_action_ids`, `/runtime`, canonical runtime commands, and primary approval action identity from the blocked episode rather than `request_id`. A surviving `request_id` is lineage or compatibility metadata for historical replay, not the primary approval action target.

A blocked episode covers approval waiting, clarification waiting, auth `/prerequisite` waiting, permission `/FileSafe/external-side-effect` blocks, and worktree conflict or dirty-worktree blocks without replacing the underlying concern, receipt, or runtime object.
Blocked-episode routes identify `object_kind = blocked_episode`, `project_id`, `focused_run_id = run_id`, `object_id = blocked_sequence`, and object scope = node_id within run.

Route overrides MUST override target object identity, explicit destination surface when the action names a different surface, and scope required to make the target meaningful, including `project_id`, `thread_id`, `focused_run_id`, an explicitly requested panel, and `/tab`.
External or persisted transport is a narrowed serializable form that decodes into `route_target`, and `resume_url` is one concrete transport instance of that form.
Restore `project_id` first, then route scope such as `focused_run_id` and `thread_id` when present. Normalize every special-case id into `subject_id` or `object_kind` + `object_id`.
`OpenSubject(subject_id = artifact:...)` resolves to real document source when one exists, otherwise it resolves to transient `generated://<artifact_id>` source opening.

For non-persisted drafts, transient `generated://<artifact_id>` buffers are valid; deep-plan plus embedded-document flows expect source, `/preview/editor`, and editor surfaces to work before final persist.
`generated://<artifact_id>` is ephemeral source-buffer transport; canonical persisted identity remains `artifact:<artifact_id>` / `artifact_id`.
That block must expose `/fallback`, `/effective`, and account-switch disclosures, preserve `requested_account_policy`, and define a requested-side concrete account anchor.
Historical run, usage, approval, and recovery records preserve the requested-side concrete account or binding/policy evidence beside the effective account chosen for execution.

Fields include `switch_event_id`, `project_id`, `provider_id`, optional `execution_role?`, optional `requested_account_id?`, optional `requested_account_binding?`, optional `from_account_id?`, optional `to_account_id?`, `switch_reason`, `decision_kind`, optional `source_episode_id?`, optional `run_id?`, optional `attempt_id?`, optional `thread_id?`, and `ts`; `decision_kind` is closed to `switched | stayed | blocked_no_backup | blocked_required_account | failed`.

Canonical requested-side fields include `requested_account_id?`, `requested_account_binding?`, and a usage record extension with `account_switch_reason?` plus `switch_event_ref?` or equivalent durable linkage.

`orchestrator.receipt.{run_id}.{attempt_id}` and `orchestrator.receipt` records are keyed by `run_id` and `attempt_id`, `usage_record` carries `attempt_id?`, run-graph and `/orchestrator` projections require attempt-level resolution.

Executor-facing docs and dispatch payloads require the runtime attribution packet: `run_id`, `thread_id?`, `node_id?`, `attempt_id?`, `execution_role?`, `provider_attempt_ref?`, and `usage_event_ref?`.

Required fields are `attention_item_id`, `project_id`, `severity`, `owner_kind`, `reason_code`, `source_kind`, `source_object_ref`, either `primary_route_payload_ref` or an inline route payload, optional `secondary_route_payload`, `projection_trust_state`, `dismissibility_kind`, optional `quiet_until_utc`, `active`, `created_at_utc`, `updated_at_utc`, and optional `resolved_at_utc`.

`storage-plan` / `storage-plan.md` owns `/health`, `/refresh`, `/projection`, `project_summary`, `project_attention_item`, account pressure/switch episode records, projector refresh semantics, and fallback rules; Contracts keeps the shared field grammar while storage owns persistence and projection mechanics.

Legacy `success | failed | ceiling_exceeded` and current `fixed | superseded | abandoned | replan_required` values must be represented through an explicit compatibility mapping, with `ceiling_exceeded` and `replan_required` retained as named outcomes.

`superseded` and `replan_required` remain graph patch and generation-lineage states, `abandoned` is not the same as simple `failed`, and a generic `failed` outcome cannot erase the reason needed to explain the historical projection.

Remediation should use one canonical resolution family, and the lineage-aware form is preferred over a coarse `success` / `/failed` enum when replay or repair lineage matters. Shared `/effective/provider/account` disclosure is reusable across auth events, usage records, graph details, artifacts, and blocked `/recovery` records.

`GATE-010` must eventually validate more than flat wiring coverage: command wrapper normalization, `route_target` pass-through, `OpenSubject` subject-open binding, and deprecated alias versus stable wrapper semantics are part of the Contracts-owned proof shape.

Direct command dispatch verification must also encode wrapper normalization, deprecated alias mapping, route/open contract consumption, and command classification such as `shell_view` versus `navigation_wrapper`.
Identity-native objects use the section 7.4 `OpenSubject` contract with `subject_id` and `open_intent`.

`OpenSubject` is identity plus open intent, not storage metadata and not shell routing. If `OpenSubject` carries panel/tab/shell destination semantics or `/tab/shell` state, it collapses into a second route contract; destination class stays in required `target_kind`.
Route activation may reuse persisted project `/surface` state only when the route omits a destination-local override and reuse still reveals the requested target.

Stable account identity normalization must preserve the hard realm split between `github_api` and `copilot_github`; model/provider contracts and downstream projection payloads must also split transport host identity from upstream `/provider` identity.

It must not encode panel widths, floating window coordinates, icon order, or full project-state snapshots; `/workspace` and project context are routing scope, while layout realization stays shell state.
Stable wrappers set `normalizes_to_contract`; deprecated aliases set `alias_of_command_id`; command execution normalizes to the canonical route/open contract rather than a command-local target model.
Concern is a first-class durable record distinct from review finding, annotation, blocked episode, and graph patch request.
Use active/acknowledged/resolved/dismissed as concern lifecycle states.

Relevant `tool.invoked`, `tool.denied`, runtime artifact payloads, operational receipt records, and `/bridge` records carry `operational_identity?` whenever side effects occur, so provider/account/permission posture remains attributable across attempts.

An effective-resolution record must carry `execution_role`, operational identity / side-effect target identity, and requested concrete account binding fields rather than relying on nearby runtime prose.

`degraded-trust` is represented as a cross-surface concern/projection-trust state. Contracts consumers MUST route degraded-trust/account-health concern escalation through the shared concern record, blocked-owner, and escalation-ladder model instead of inventing surface-local warning aliases.
Tier boundaries are not approval scope anchors. Approval and recovery pivots normalize to `/node/blocked` runtime scope with blocked-episode identity anchored by run/node/blocked sequence.
